Theorem
[Solution of wave equation in even dimensions] ↗ thm:wave-equation-odd-dimensions-solution 1. ch2:2.4-thm-3\group Wave Equation

Let $n\ge 2$ be even, $m=(n+2)/2$, $g\in C^{m+1}(\R ^n)$, and $h\in C^m(\R ^n)$. The function (38) belongs to $C^2(\R ^n\times [0,\infty ))$, solves $u_{tt}-\Delta u=0$, and satisfies \[ u(x,t)\to g(x^0), \qquad u_t(x,t)\to h(x^0) \] as $(x,t)\to (x^0,0)$ with $t>0$.
Proof

\sketch Apply subsubsection thm:wave-equation-odd-dimensions-solution in dimension $n+1$ to the extensions independent of the final coordinate. Parametrizing the two hemispheres reduces the spherical averages to the weighted ball integrals in (38), and restriction to the hyperplane recovers $u$.

□
